brief.scope: Security-only recheck of revised discovery docs against supplied Daybreak findings and conductor ruling. Assess whether trusted repository/gitdir anchoring, closed startup source graph, tracked bounded enumeration, complete selection metadata/fingerprints, profile/lineage relevance, untrusted-content treatment and overflow behavior resolve the previously demonstrated contract ambiguities. Include new source adapters and conductor/worker role boundary in that focused review. Test reasoning against nominal/negative cases without inventing a broader threat model or demanding future implementation in this docs slice. No edits, executable test authoring, source/settings/host/DB/network changes or real harness launches. Return <=800-word verdict with resolved/unresolved prior keys, concrete expected/found/needed for remaining issues, changed-document locations and checks. Distinguish contract-level ambiguities from observed runtime vulnerabilities. Functional acceptance is separately reviewed.

findings.claim: Expected conductor/worker source grants to be non-substitutable trusted launch capabilities. Found the contract claims a trusted descriptor and worker isolation, but preserves a CLI whose caller selects --config FILE; the existing entrypoint loads that path, and no rule binds it to launch identity. A worker invoking the shared CLI with a readable conductor config can obtain sources outside its job, contradicting D-A42. This is a contract ambiguity, not an observed runtime exploit. Needed: require an inherited/pinned capability or authenticated wrapper that makes the configuration non-replaceable, and require alternate worker-supplied configurations to refuse before source access.

findings.claim: Expected prior hostile-content key 5 to place record prose behind a consumer-facing boundary before the MCP/model seam. Found the exact Candidate carries the hostile body verbatim, tools/resources project that envelope, and the transport returns it directly as text and structuredContent. Requiring an unspecified later renderer to escape delimiters occurs after the content has reached the MCP consumer. Needed: define projection-owned pre-transport delimiting/encoding with exact collision escaping, or omit body from MCP; make D-A32 verify the literal tool/resource result.

envelope.note: Prior Daybreak keys 1 root/gitdir anchoring, 2 closed source composition, 3 complete snapshots, 4 profile/lineage relevance, and 6 deterministic overflow are resolved at contract level. Prior key 5 remains unresolved; the role/source-grant issue is additionally unresolved. Nominal and negative clauses now cover tracked enumeration, Git output/type checks, races, identical-blob ref movement, special files, and bounded failures. No executable, SQL, template, dependency, lockfile, fetched-action, or workflow file changed; common credential/private-key/token patterns were absent, and captured records expose credential filenames only. Record sandbox labels matched recorded argv or explicitly said policy containment. Runtime behavior, actual descriptor confinement, renderer behavior, filesystem races, and sandbox enforcement could not be covered because v3 is absent and launches/mutations were prohibited.
